title: OOM repro + tensorcore/driver mismatch playbook
body:
Context and goal:
- Flaky OOMs hitting nightly inference job when batching > 8 on A100-80GB nodes (k8s pool: inference-large). Sporadic: some runs succeed, others OOM in first few forward steps. Suspect a driver / lib mismatch or tensorcore-specific kernel fallback issue.

Observed symptoms (raw snippets captured):
- Python stack (trace from failed run):
  File "/app/serve/runner.py", line 132, in forward_batch
    out = model(inputs)
  RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 512.00 MiB (GPU 0; 79.68 GiB total capacity; 78.43 GiB already allocated; 64.00 MiB free; 78.58 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)

- Immediately before (container logs):
  WARNING:root:ATen: cuda generator is not the same as Host generator (expected?), falling back to slower path
  torch.cuda.current_device() -> 0
  torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory -> 85899345920

- dmesg (host) around same time: 
  [Jan28 12:03:41] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: firmware: failed to load nvidia/vid_ch11_firmware.bin (-2)
  [Jan28 12:03:42] nvidia-mig: failed to create device uuid 6141f...: -22
  [Jan28 12:03:43] Out of memory: Kill process 23456 (python) score 1024 or sacrifice child

- nvidia-smi snapshot (when job crashes):
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12    Driver Version: 525.85.12    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
  | GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
  |  0  NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB  On  | 0000:3b:00.0     Off |                  0 |
  |  0%   78C    P0   3581W / 400W |   78800MiB / 81920MiB |     0%      Default |
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

- container runtime: docker 24.0 + nvidia-container-toolkit 2.12.0. Image built with CUDA 12.1 runtime libraries (libcudart.so.12, libcuda.so.1 from host mounted).

Commands I've run (notes + outputs):
- Basic sanity: nvidia-smi, + top, free -g -> looked fine, GPU showing heavy allocation before crash.
- ldd on libcudart in container: ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.12 -> resolves to host libcuda via /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (symlink)
- readelf -s libcuda.so.1 | grep cuCtxGetCurrent -> symbol present.
- docker run --gpus all --rm -it image bash -> inside: python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available())' -> "12.1 True"
- Repro script (minimal):
  import torch
  m = torch.nn.Linear(10240, 10240).cuda()
  x = torch.randn(256, 10240, device='cuda')
  for i in range(1000):
      y = m(x)
      torch.cuda.synchronize()
  # intermittent OOM after ~20-400 iterations depending on run

- Checked driver vs toolkit pairing: driver 525.x is in supported range for CUDA 12.1 but 525.x is borderline for some A100 firmware features. Also saw firmware missing message in dmesg earlier.

- lsof /dev/nvidia* (host) during run -> container has several fds but some ubuntu host processes also hold fds to /dev/nvidiactl intermittently. Possibly other tenants on same host? This is a dedicated node pool but autoscaler may have system pods.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Driver+firmware mismatch causing intermittent failing kernels that don't release memory (seen firmware load error + MIG create fail in dmesg). When kernel falls back from tensor-core optimized path to slower path, memory accounting may be inconsistent.
2) PyTorch/CUDA runtime bug: double-reservation due to allocator and CUDART mismatch (container libs vs driver versions). ldd shows host libcuda used, but image CUDA runtime is 12.1; combination might be okay but there are edgecases.
3) Persistent kernel from previous job (residual allocations) due to nvidia-persistenced not enabled in this node image -> memory fragmentation over time.
4) NCCL/collectives creating large GPU buffers transiently at startup of the batch (less likely for single-process local test).

Actions tried so far (what changed, and outcome):
- Restarted nvidia-persistenced -> no reliable fix.
- Rebooted node -> one run succeeded, then later failed again after ~6 runs. Suggests stateful or workload-dependent.
- Forced container to use host libstdc++/libgcc (to reduce C++ ABI mismatches) -> no change.
- Switched image to pytorch built with cudatoolkit=12.0 (instead of 12.1) -> still reproduced, though frequency reduced.
- Upgraded nvidia-container-toolkit to 2.13.0 on one node -> no repro there across 12 hours (promising).
- Upgraded driver on a canary node to 545.61 -> no repro across 24 hours with same load.

Repro notes / minimal reproduction plan:
- Use a canary node with driver 525.85 (current fleet) and the failing image. Launch 8 parallel containers each doing the minimal repro script with batch size 256 and sleep between iterations 0.1s.
- Collect: dmesg -wH, journalctl -f, nvidia-smi -l 1, docker logs, and capture /proc/$(pid)/maps and /proc/$(pid)/smaps for python process at crash. Also run 'nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv -l 1' to correlate pids.

Useful commands to run next (one-liners):
- inspect driver vs cuda libs:
  python - <<PY
  import ctypes, torch, os
  print('torch cuda:', torch.version.cuda)
  libcudart = ctypes.CDLL('libcudart.so.12')
  print('cudart version', ctypes.c_int.in_dll(libcudart, 'cudaRuntimeGetVersion'))
  PY
- check lib mismatch quickly in container:
  for f in /usr/local/cuda/lib64/*.so*; do echo; echo $f; ldd $f | egrep 'not found|libcuda'; done
- snapshot kernel messages before crash: sudo dmesg -T --level=err,warn | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-snapshot.txt
- enable persistence mode and reset GPU between runs: sudo nvidia-smi -pm 1; sudo nvidia-smi -r

Next steps / action items: 
- (Priya) Reproduce on node with upgraded driver (545) and collect long-run traces to assert non-repro.
- (Evan) Attempt to run the minimal repro inside an OCI runtime with "--ipc=host" vs default to see if shared IPC changes allocator behavior.
- (Jules) Open bug with PyTorch team with attached reproducer + exact libcudart/libcuda pairing and dmesg. Include the 'nvidia-firmware missing' log lines.
- Fleet action: schedule driver roll-forward for inference-large pool to >= 545.xx, but gate rollout behind canary tests.

Loose notes / observations:
- Saw a single message on one host: "nvidia: failed to find symbol 'cuptiActivityEnable' in libcupti.so" -- indicates some cupti mismatch in image (not used by runtime but present).
- Container was built by CI with multi-stage: base cuda:12.1-cudnn8 -> we overlay pip wheel torch+cu121. Possibly wheel expects slightly newer driver.
- Fragmentation pattern: successive small allocations spike reserved memory (PyTorch caching allocator), but total 'allocated' reported in error is huge -> suggests a leak or another process holding memory. Check pids via nvidia-smi at time.

Short-term mitigation for customers:
- Fall back to smaller batch sizes (<=4) if latency can tolerate, or set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False and forcing deterministic algos to avoid tensorcore heuristics.
- Add pre-flight: run small cuda malloc/free probe at job start to ensure driver can allocate small buffers on all GPUs: python -c 'import torch; x=torch.empty(1, device="cuda"); del x; torch.cuda.empty_cache()' and fail fast with clear error to trigger auto-retry on a different node.

Files to attach to GH bug / Jira:
- /tmp/dmesg-snapshot.txt (dmesg + firmware lines)
- nvidia-smi csv log (pid,mem) across time
- minimal repro reproducer (python file)

Anything I missed? Open to ideas: possibly PCI-E error recovery, but I don't see AER logs besides firmware. Also consider kernel driver ABI mismatch (dkms vs packaged nvidia).

Triage status: collecting long-run traces on canary nodes, preparing artifacts to open PyTorch/driver bugs.

-- end of scratchpad (will update with new traces)
